data.description:
# DC one-way segmenting wiki renderer

## Context / Problem
Jira Data Center stores rich text as wiki markup, a lossy text format. No library round-trips rebar's punctuation-dense prose: pandoc's jira reader misparses `->`, ASCII pipe-tables, and regex, and provably erodes them one character per pass (the ASCII-table body decays 9115→9110 monotonically). Whole-body all-or-nothing conversion is echo-safe but only ~15% rich. A **segmenting** one-way renderer that converts only structurally-safe units and passes dangerous ones through verbatim reaches ~68% of bodies / ~78% of chars rich, proven non-corrupting across 23 environments, 6 authors, and an out-of-distribution corpus.

## Approach
Render **one way** (MD→wiki); echo-safety is provided by the separate state-suppression story, so this codec does NOT need to be a fixed point. Pipeline: split the body into blocks and list-items; for each unit, render structurally-safe units (headings, lists, code, quotes, safe paragraphs) to wiki via pinned `pandoc` (`-f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none`); pass dangerous units (ASCII tables, arrow/regex/HTML-dense prose) through **verbatim**; reassemble. Two lossless wins run as render rules: **code-aware arrow substitution** (`-> <- <-> =>` → `→ ← ↔ ⇒`, prose-only, skipping fenced/inline code) which MUST run on the **Markdown before pandoc** (after pandoc, code is already `{{…}}` and prose `->` is already escaped, so a post-render pass misfires); and **verbatim-wrapping ASCII tables in `{noformat}`** to stop the per-pass dash erosion. Wire into the DC backend (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py`, `normalize_rich_text` at line 131). Ship **descriptions before comments** (descriptions convert 100% some-rich / 30% chars vs comments 63% / 23.6%).

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` — outbound MD→wiki render entry point.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — new segmenting renderer module (split → per-unit safe-render/passthrough → reassemble; arrow substitution; table wrap).
- `pyproject.toml` — pinned `pypandoc` extra.
- `tests/` — segmenting/arrow/table corpus tests.

## Testing
- Happy path: a description of headings + a checklist + a fenced code block renders to wiki `h1.`/`*`-bullets/`{code}` and reassembles in original order.
- Danger passthrough: a body containing an ASCII pipe-table and a prose `->` and a `obj->method()` code arrow renders with the table verbatim in `{noformat}`, prose `->`→`→`, and the code arrow untouched.
- Corpus coverage/safety: over the historical corpus the renderer yields rich for ~68% of bodies with 0 code-arrow rewrites and 0 prose corruptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The renderer segments a body and renders only structurally-safe units, passing dangerous units (tables/arrows/regex/HTML) through verbatim; verified by `test_dc_segmenting_passthrough` on a mixed body.
- [ ] Code-aware arrow substitution runs on the Markdown before pandoc and touches 0 code arrows; verified by a test asserting `obj->method()` is unchanged while a prose `->` becomes `→` (regression over the 179 known code-arrow bodies: 0 rewrites).
- [ ] ASCII tables are verbatim-wrapped in `{noformat}` and do not erode across passes; verified by `test_dc_table_noformat_stable` over the known erosion bodies (70/70 stable).
- [ ] Over the historical corpus the renderer produces rich output for ≈68% of bodies / ≈78% of chars with zero prose corruption; verified by `test_dc_corpus_coverage`.
data.title: DC one-way segmenting wiki renderer
